Committee of Supply debate on the Prime Minister's Office budget

Committee of Supply debate on Head U of the Estimates26 February 2026 budget-2876

A Committee of Supply debate on Head U (Prime Minister's Office) of the Estimates, with MPs moving cuts and ministers responding on public service, research and innovation, climate policy, population, cash and banking access, and insurance.

The transcript states that the carbon tax has increased to $45 per tonne this year, that households will receive additional U-Save rebates to manage energy costs, and that HDB has given the go-ahead for DBS to set up an ATM at Rivervale Shores. It also records that MAS is monitoring cash acceptance and may consider making cash acceptance mandatory by law.

Ministry of Finance Committee of Supply debate on fiscal stewardship, tax thresholds and procurement

Committee of Supply26 February 2026 budget-2877

A Committee of Supply debate on Head M (Ministry of Finance), where MPs moved cuts to the allocation and ministers responded on fiscal policy, tax, procurement and business support.

The record sets out changes for businesses: Tender Lite for ICT procurement will launch from April 2026, and all GST-registered businesses must submit digital invoices via InvoiceNow by April 2031. For individuals, the Minister said the $20,000 personal income tax exemption threshold will be regularly reviewed, and the GST display concession for F&B and hotels will be reviewed in future. The amendment to reduce Head M by $100 was withdrawn.

      Verbatim

    • Raised the long-standing provision exempting the first $20,000 of chargeable income from tax and called for periodic review of structural thresholds.

      Verbatim
      the long-standing provision that effectively exempts the first $20,000 of chargeable income from tax

      Verbatim

What happens next Mr Saktiandi Supaat withdrew his amendment. MOF will launch Tender Lite for ICT procurement from April 2026; all GST-registered businesses must submit digital invoices via InvoiceNow by April 2031; ACRA will consult later this year; IRAS and IMDA will release more details on the InvoiceNow timeline and support; and the GST display concession will be reviewed in future.

Parliament debates Budget 2026

Budget debate24 February 2026 – 26 February 2026 budget-2859, budget-2857, budget-2861, budget-2867

A parliamentary debate on Budget 2026, with MPs speaking and the Prime Minister responding to clarifications.

MPs said Budget 2026 continues one-off support such as CDC vouchers and utilities rebates, and strengthens CPF top-ups and higher contribution rates for seniors. They also said it raises the monthly household income threshold for student care fee assistance to $6,500 and lowers PARF rebates by 45% with a $30,000 cap. The transcript records many further proposals, but does not state that they have been adopted.

Open questions from this debate (12)

Questions the debate raises that the record does not resolve. Listed as open questions, not as findings.

  • Whether the Government will adopt the proposed changes to CDC voucher distribution.
  • Whether the $20,000 income tax exemption threshold will be reviewed or adjusted.
  • Whether the SkillsFuture Jobseeker Support Scheme income threshold will be raised.
  • Whether advance retrenchment notification will be agreed by the tripartite partners.
  • Whether transitional relief will be provided for car buyers affected by the PARF rebate changes.
  • Whether dental care will be integrated into Healthier SG.
  • Whether Personal Learning Devices will be extended to primary school students.
  • Whether estate duty or a Net Annual Value tax will be reintroduced.
  • Whether the Government will commit to annual reporting of AI value creation, productivity and wage uplift outcomes.
  • Whether adoption leave will be aligned with maternity leave at 16 weeks.
  • Whether the Silver Support per capita household income criterion will be removed or reviewed.
  • Whether the Government will increase subsidies for assisted reproductive treatments.

How this page was made

Built from the official Hansard record (Parliament of Singapore Official Reports). No news reporting was used. Briefs are written by software from the transcript and every key point carries the verbatim words it was drawn from.

  • Reports collected: 75 (complete)
  • Briefs on this page: 3 (136 verified points)
  • Speaker attribution: 98% of turns carry an explicit speaker tag
  • Any point whose quote could not be found in the transcript was discarded rather than shown.
